correctness.rationale: Exhaustive graph/face definition checks on \(2^{16}\) masks, all 519328 oriented Hasse incidences, an acyclic matching with critical counts (1,13,2) in dimensions (0,11,12), and an independently recomputed signed 13x2 Morse boundary with a unit 2x2 minor give Smith factors (1,1). The degree-11 Hurewicz isomorphism and elementary CW cancellation yield exactly eleven 11-spheres. Independent dual finite-field ranks cross-check but do not replace this integral proof.

evidence: Bayer et al. treat forests, cycles, multipartite graphs and clique prisms; Theorem 6.1 requires the complete codimension-one skeleton, which is absent here because 60 complementary 4-sets avoid disconnected triples.
Topology of Cut Complexes II explicitly treats rectangular path grids and squared paths; the Shrikhande graph is neither.
Published rook graph three-cut homology gives rank 27 for the 4x4 case; its proof relies on clique-row/column and rectangle decomposition absent from the Shrikhande graph.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The strongest same-cut prior record covers the nonisomorphic rook graph, not the Shrikhande graph. Shared (16,6,2,2) parameters enforce equal counts of connected triples but not the higher-face structure of their duals: 44 versus 60 dual tetrahedra, with consequently different homology. Neither paper provides a stronger theorem forcing this finite homotopy type.

value.rationale: The canonical Shrikhande and 4x4 rook strongly regular twins have identical (16,6,2,2) parameters and the same number of connected triples but different natural 3-cut topology: integral degree-11 ranks 11 and 27. The distinction arises from 60 versus 44 four-vertex dual faces and is a meaningful exact homotopy classification of a canonical graph beyond existing known rook family results, not a routine renaming or tiny numerical improvement.
